strategy.what_why: A standalone welcome sent after contract and before travel is scheduled. Its job is to confirm the relationship, introduce the people behind it, and orient the reader without assigning them a place in the project.
strategy.for_whom: A busy general manager, IT director, or operations leader who recently signed with LUCI and needs a quick reminder of what the partnership means.
strategy.reach: Send from Michael Epstein at mepstein@lucisystems.com. Keep the note brief: personal welcome, one light line about LUCI, a neutral five-part project map, and a direct close from Mike.
strategy.impact: Sound like a CEO writing to a new partner, not a campaign explaining a product. The strongest proof is continuity: the engineers who learn the operation remain involved.
strategy.primary_message: Welcome to LUCI—you now have a real team that will learn your operation and stay with you.

directions.name: The team that stays
directions.summary: Lead with LUCI’s most human point of difference: clients keep working with the same accountable team. The retention line works as proof of that commitment rather than a sales claim.

header.headline: Welcome to the LUCI family.
header.subline: A team that learns your operation—and stays with you.

body: I wanted to personally welcome you to the LUCI family. You chose us to bring your property’s A/V operation into one interface, and we’re glad to be part of your team.
The engineers you work with aren’t a handoff team. They’re the people who will learn your operation, build the system with you, and stay involved throughout the relationship.
We’ve never lost a client. I believe that comes down to something simple: we stay.

directions.name: A note from Mike
directions.summary: Open as a direct thank-you from the CEO, then give the cold reader a one-sentence reminder of what they chose. The structure feels like a personal letter with a practical project map attached.

header.headline: Glad to have you with us.
header.subline: A personal welcome from Michael Epstein.

body: Thank you for choosing LUCI. I know bringing a new partner into your A/V operation is a meaningful decision, and I’m glad you placed that trust in us.
LUCI will give your team one interface for operating the guest experience, backed by engineers who take the time to understand your property.
Those engineers remain part of your team throughout the relationship. You’ll know who to call, and we’ll know how your operation works.
directions.process_lead_in: Here’s the general shape of a LUCI project:

steps.name: Project alignment
steps.descriptor: Define the scope, responsibilities, and technical needs.

steps.name: Technical design
steps.descriptor: Confirm the network plan and system architecture.

steps.name: System preparation
steps.descriptor: Configure the LUCI appliance and coordinate logistics.

steps.name: Property integration
steps.descriptor: Connect endpoints and verify system performance.

steps.name: Team enablement
steps.descriptor: Train your operators and maintain ongoing support.

closing: I’m looking forward to working together. If you need anything, reply directly to this email.

directions.name: Meet your LUCI team
directions.summary: Put the engineers at the center immediately. This direction makes the welcome tangible by explaining who the client will work with and how that relationship carries across the project.

header.headline: You’re part of the LUCI family.
header.subline: The people behind your project are here to stay.

body: Welcome to LUCI. I want you to know what “family” means to us: real people who learn your operation and remain accountable for the work.
The engineers who design and integrate your system are the same people who stay involved after handoff. They’ll get to know your A/V environment, your team, and the way your property operates.
LUCI brings that operation into one interface. Our team makes sure the partnership around it remains just as connected.
directions.process_lead_in: Every project is different, but the work follows five clear parts:

steps.name: Listen
steps.descriptor: Understand the operation, scope, and technical requirements.

steps.name: Design
steps.descriptor: Map the network, equipment, and system responsibilities.

steps.name: Prepare
steps.descriptor: Configure the LUCI appliance and organize site needs.

steps.name: Integrate
steps.descriptor: Connect A/V endpoints and test the full system.

steps.name: Support
steps.descriptor: Train your team and remain engaged over time.

closing: You’ll hear from the team directly as the work takes shape. My door is open, too.

why_won: It is the warmest and most credible welcome because it makes “family” mean something concrete: continuity and accountability. It borrows the cold-reader reminder from “A note from Mike” and the engineer focus from “Meet your LUCI team,” while keeping the benefit line to one sentence and the project map neutral.

preheader: A personal welcome from Mike, plus a simple look at how LUCI projects take shape.
property_merge_decision: Use “your property” and “your team” in the final. %PROPERTY% adds merge risk without making this short personal note warmer.
guardrail_audit: Pass. The final is warm, personal, active, and cold-reader clear; it contains one light benefit line, no checklist, no schedule or recipient-stage cue, and a neutral five-part process. It uses A/V correctly, mentions only a single LUCI appliance in the process, does not describe LUCI as a layer or claim broad technology replacement, and makes ongoing team support explicit. It includes no release language, named partner or customer, pricing, duration, or stacked exclamation. The retention claim is tied directly to the warm “we stay” idea. The optional portal block stands alone and makes no call or stage reference.
open_questions: Greeting merge tag: the requested copy uses “Dear #Name#,” but the ActiveCampaign template currently uses %FIRSTNAME%. Jane needs to confirm the production merge tag.
Property merge field: the final intentionally uses “your property.” Jane can choose %PROPERTY% if she prefers personalization despite the merge-field risk.
Portal block: Jane needs to decide whether Email 1 should include it. Emails 5 and 8 already offer portal access, and Email 2 refers to the LUCI support site.
Retention claim: “We’ve never lost a client” is prominent and warm here, but it remains an objective public-facing claim that Jane should confirm before production use.
